q: What storage configuration does EKS Auto Mode handle automatically?

opts.b: Volume types, volume sizes, encryption policies, and deletion policies upon node termination

exp.a: Incorrect. EKS Auto Mode configures more than just volume sizes.
exp.b: Correct. EKS Auto Mode configures ephemeral storage by setting up volume types, volume sizes, encryption policies, and deletion policies upon node termination. [6]
exp.c: Incorrect. More than just encryption is managed.
exp.d: Incorrect. The configuration is more comprehensive than just provisioning.

q: Do you need to install the EKS Pod Identity Agent on EKS Auto Mode clusters?

opts.a: Yes, it must be installed as a DaemonSet
opts.b: Yes, it must be installed as an add-on
opts.c: No, you do not have to install it on EKS Auto Mode clusters

exp.a: Incorrect. Manual DaemonSet installation is not required.
exp.b: Incorrect. Add-on installation is not required.
exp.c: Correct. You do not have to install the EKS Pod Identity Agent on EKS Auto Mode clusters—it is pre-installed by default. [6]
exp.d: Incorrect. It's pre-installed regardless of whether session policies are used.

q: A company needs to run EKS workloads and wants AWS to handle node provisioning, OS patching, and component updates. They want to focus only on their application containers. Which EKS feature should they use?

opts.b: EKS Auto Mode

exp.a: Incorrect. Managed Node Groups still require some node management.
exp.b: Correct. EKS Auto Mode streamlines EKS management by providing production-ready clusters with minimal operational overhead, letting customers concentrate on application-specific concerns while delegating cluster infrastructure management to AWS. [6]
exp.c: Incorrect. Fargate is serverless but doesn't cover all workload types.
exp.d: Incorrect. Self-managed nodes require the most operational effort.

q: An EKS Auto Mode cluster detects that an Availability Zone is impaired. What happens automatically?

opts.b: All pods are terminated
opts.c: Auto Mode stops provisioning nodes in the impaired AZ and suspends voluntary disruption via ARC zonal shift integration
opts.d: Nothing; the user must manually intervene

exp.a: Incorrect. The cluster doesn't shut down.
exp.b: Incorrect. Pods on healthy AZs continue running.
exp.c: Correct. EKS Auto Mode integrates with Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) zonal shift to automatically stop provisioning nodes in an impaired AZ and suspend voluntary disruption during a zonal shift event. [6]
exp.d: Incorrect. The response is automatic via ARC integration.

q: Where does Amazon EKS recommend you view your current service quotas?

opts.b: The AWS Management Console (Service Quotas)

exp.a: Incorrect. While CLI works, AWS recommends the console.
exp.b: Correct. AWS recommends using the AWS Management Console to view your current quotas through the Service Quotas console. [13]
exp.c: Incorrect. The EKS API doesn't directly display service quotas.
exp.d: Incorrect. CloudFormation doesn't display service quotas.

q: A company has many EKS workloads interacting with various AWS services and is encountering throttling issues. What is the root cause according to AWS best practices?

opts.b: AWS service quotas and request throttling limits being reached

exp.a: Incorrect. Pod count alone doesn't cause throttling.
exp.b: Correct. Customer workloads can encounter AWS service quotas and request throttling issues that hamper scalability. Your AWS account has default quotas that are generally region-specific. [11]
exp.c: Incorrect. Node capacity is a separate issue from API throttling.
exp.d: Incorrect. Network bandwidth is different from API request throttling.

q: Which services can AWS Fargate run containers for?

opts.b: Amazon EKS only
opts.c: Both Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS

exp.a: Incorrect. Fargate also supports EKS.
exp.b: Incorrect. Fargate also supports ECS.
exp.c: Correct. You pay for resources consumed by your containerized applications running on Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS) or Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS). [14]
exp.d: Incorrect. Lambda is a separate serverless compute service.

q: A company using EKS Auto Mode wants to add a custom per-node feature that isn't included in Auto Mode's managed components. How can they do this?

opts.a: It's not possible with Auto Mode
opts.b: Through AWS add-ons that provide optional per-node features

exp.a: Incorrect. Additional features can be added.
exp.b: Correct. Optional per-node features can be included in clusters through AWS add-ons. [6]
exp.c: Incorrect. SSH access is blocked on Bottlerocket AMIs used by Auto Mode.
exp.d: Incorrect. Bottlerocket has immutable root file systems.
